concepts.why: The patient's history of discharge through the artificial ear canal and the presence of a hypodense lesion in the middle ear suggest chronic suppurative otitis media.
The hyperintense lesion at the edge of the petrous bone and the presence of a fistula originating from the middle ear suggest petrous bone osteomyelitis.
The patient's history of neck cellulitis and the presence of a fistula at the tip of the mastoid suggest mastoiditis.
The presence of a millimetric fistula at the tip of the mastoid running into the sternocleidomastoid muscle suggests a sternocleidomastoid muscle abscess.
The patient's history of unilateral otomandibular syndrome associated with severe temporal bone hypoplasia suggests OMS.
The patient's history of temporal bone hypoplasia suggests TBH.
The presence of a fistula originating from the middle ear suggests a fistula of the middle ear.
The patient's history of surgical complications and the presence of a millimetric fistula at the tip of the mastoid suggest a surgical complication of mastoidectomy.
